BOAS surgery for English bulldogs in Los Angeles

By Dr. Antonio Pedraza, MRCVS · Updated 20 August 2026

BOAS surgery for English bulldogs is a set of airway procedures (nostril widening and soft-palate shortening) that reduces breathing effort in brachycephalic dogs. In Los Angeles it costs between 3,500 and 6,000 USD and most dogs go home the same day.

What does BOAS surgery involve?

The procedure has two standard parts: alar fold resection to widen stenotic nares, and staphylectomy to shorten an elongated soft palate. Surgery takes 45 to 90 minutes under general anaesthesia.

In about 30% of dogs a third step, removal of everted laryngeal saccules, is added when they obstruct the airway. Each step is decided during the same anaesthetic after direct examination of the larynx.

  • Nares: 10-15 minutes
  • Soft palate: 20-40 minutes
  • Saccules: 10 minutes

How much does BOAS surgery cost in Los Angeles?

In Los Angeles the full procedure costs between 3,500 and 6,000 USD in 2026, including anaesthesia, one night of monitoring and the first follow-up visit. Pre-surgical bloodwork adds 150 to 300 USD.

ItemRange (USD)
Surgery3,500-6,000
Bloodwork150-300

How long is recovery after BOAS surgery?

Most bulldogs breathe noticeably better within 48 hours and return to normal activity in 14 days. Swelling of the soft palate peaks at 24 to 72 hours, which is why the first two nights are the highest-risk period.

Soft food for 10 days and no collar pressure for 2 weeks are the two rules owners must follow. A recheck at day 14 confirms healing of the palate.

What are the risks of BOAS surgery?

Serious complications occur in fewer than 5% of cases according to a 2022 study of 300 dogs published by the Royal Veterinary College. The main risks are post-operative swelling, aspiration pneumonia and regurgitation during the first 72 hours.

Older dogs (over 6 years) and dogs with laryngeal collapse grade 2 or 3 carry a higher risk, which is why staging the larynx before surgery matters.

Sources

Data from the Royal Veterinary College BOAS research group and the AVMA.
